clauses.reason: The title and enacting words of EO 11095 state the order's subject, assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Board of Directors of the Tennessee Valley Authority, the Railroad Retirement Board, the Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, the Federal Power Commission and the Director of the National Science Foundation, and the authority under which the President acted, including Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958; they operate only through the numbered sections that follow, so they ended with the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 1 of EO 11095 directs the five named agency heads, referred to collectively as Heads of agencies, to prepare national emergency plans and develop preparedness programs covering the functions assigned to them in the order, designed to develop a state of readiness for all conditions of national emergency. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 2 of EO 11095 directs the Board of Directors of the Tennessee Valley Authority to carry out functions set out in lettered paragraphs on electric power, waterways, flood control, health and sanitary water supplies, coordination of water use, munitions production, land management, radiological monitoring, food and forestry, and coordination with Valley States. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 3 of EO 11095 directs the Railroad Retirement Board to carry out manpower functions, within the framework of the manpower plans of the Department of Labor, and benefit payment functions, assisting the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 4 of EO 11095 directs the Administrator of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration to adapt and use the Administration's scientific and technological capability to meet priority needs of Federal programs in an emergency, including research and development, and to provide military support. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 5 of EO 11095 directs the Federal Power Commission to assist the Department of the Interior in connection with emergency preparedness functions with respect to electric power and natural gas as specified in an agreement between the Secretary of the Interior and the Chairman of the Commission. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 6 of EO 11095 directs the Director of the National Science Foundation to carry out manpower functions, assisting the Department of Labor, and special functions. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 7 of EO 11095 directs the Heads of agencies, as appropriate and in consonance with the national civil defense plans, programs and operations of the Department of Defense under Executive Order No. 10952, to provide facilities protection guidance material and to carry out damage assessment. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 8 of EO 11095 directs the Heads of agencies, within the framework of Federal research objectives, to supervise or conduct research in areas directly concerned with carrying out emergency preparedness responsibilities, to designate representatives for necessary ad hoc or task force groups, and to provide advice and assistance to other agencies in planning for research in areas involving each agency's interest. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 9 of EO 11095 directs each agency to provide for appropriate participation in the national resources evaluation program administered by the Office of Emergency Planning. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 10 of EO 11095 directs the Heads of agencies to prepare plans to claim materials, manpower, equipment, supplies and services needed in support of assigned responsibilities and other essential functions of the agencies, and to work with the appropriate agencies on programs to insure availability of such resources in an emergency. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 11 of EO 11095 sets the guidance by which the Heads of agencies, in carrying out the functions assigned in the order, are to be guided: interagency cooperation (coordinating with departments and agencies having related functions), Presidential coordination (the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning is to advise and assist the President), and emergency planning (plans, programs and organization are to be developed as an integral part of each agency's continuing activities, and the Heads of agencies are to be prepared to implement all appropriate plans developed under the order). It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 12 of EO 11095 provides that nothing in the order is to be construed as conferring authority under Title III of the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950, as amended, or otherwise, to put into effect any emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course of action prepared or developed pursuant to the order, and states that such authority is reserved to the President. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

Section 13 of EO 11095 authorizes the Heads of agencies to redelegate within their agencies the functions assigned to them in the order. It was a continuing provision of the order. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

The first sentence of Section 14 of EO 11095 provides that, to the extent of any inconsistency between the provisions of any prior order and the provisions of this order, the latter controls. That rule was a continuing command and stayed in force while the order did. No end of its own appears in the held text of EO 11095: it states no expiry date or condition for this provision. It ended on 1969-10-28 when EO 11490 revoked the whole order: Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 (American Presidency Project transcription) provides, after the words "The following are hereby revoked:", item (22), "Executive Order No. 11095 of February 26, 1963.". Sec. 3014 of EO 11490 preserves existing assignments only "Except as provided by Section 3015", so it does not save this provision.

The remaining sentence of Section 14 of EO 11095 revokes Emergency Preparedness Orders No. 11, 13 and 14, issued earlier by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization. It is a one-time act that was complete when the order was issued; nothing in it continued afterwards. The held text of EO 11095, signed John F. Kennedy on February 26, 1963 at the White House, carries the revocation, so it was performed on that date (no later event is needed). The order as a whole was later revoked on 1969-10-28, but this one-time act had been completed on 1963-02-26.

research_rationale:
EO 11095 (1963-02-26; Assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Board of Directors of the Tennessee Valley Authority and four other agencies) was read in full from the held Federal Register text (28 FR 1859, Federal Register of 1963-02-28), whose file also contains neighbouring material; the order was delimited by its heading and the John F. Kennedy signature line. The dossier's machine segmentation, which cuts sections into lettered fragments and repeats some, was replaced by 16 scopes: one for the enacting words and one for each numbered section. Section 14 is split in two: its first sentence (precedence over inconsistent prior orders) and its closing sentence, which revokes Emergency Preparedness Orders No. 11, 13 and 14, issued earlier by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization. Its own terms contain no end date, expiry or termination condition. It ended on 1969-10-28 by express revocation in EO 11490, Sec. 3015, item (22), cited from the American Presidency Project transcription (APP node 255823; page record checked: heading, date and text hash agree with the held text) and read for corroboration in the Federal Register print of 34 FR 17567 onward (OCR text), which lists the same order. No amendment, suspension or other instrument naming it is held besides EO 11490, which revokes it. The selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog) are coverage statements read before use; they are leads, not independent review.

savings.reason: Item (22) of Sec. 3015 of EO 11490 revokes EO 11095. In the held American Presidency Project transcription, Sec. 3014 reads: "Except as provided by Section 3015, nothing in this order shall be deemed to derogate from any now existing assignment of functions to any department or agency or officer thereof made by statute, Executive order, or Presidential directives, including Memoranda." Because Sec. 3014 begins with that exception, it does not preserve the revoked order. The end source span cited for this claim runs from "SECTION 501. Functions." through Sec. 3015, that is Parts 5 through 30 of EO 11490. I read Sec. 3014 and Sec. 3015; I did not read the other Parts to decide whether any of them carries this order's commands forward, so no transfer or accrual is claimed and the state is none_after_bounded_search.
